correctness.rationale: A decisive false sentence in original RESULT.md was discovered: it says for n>=5 the equation (n-1)(2^p-1)=s^p has a UNIQUE positive root. For n=5,s=3, F(0)=-1, F(1)=1 and F(4)=-21, so by continuity it has two positive roots. The original finding cannot pass unchanged. A complete corrected RESULT.md has been written: it specifies the LEAST positive root (unique in (0,1)) and explicitly warns that a second F-root above the G boundary cannot restore negative type. Re-assessment of the FINAL corrected theorem: exact zero-sum block decomposition yields eigenvalues F=(n-1)(2^p-1)-s^p (dim1), G=s^p-2^p-1 (dim n-1), H=1-2^p-s^p<0 (dim n-1). Q_s=s^p/(2^p-1) strictly decreases until the first G root; at G=0, F=(n-2)2^g-n, locating the n=3 interior crossing and n=4 endpoint. For n>=5 the first F root lies in (0,1), so later F roots do not alter the p-negative-type interval. Centering gives the stated endpoint Gram ranks. Independently diagonalized the exact powered-distance block matrices at n3 A=3,B=4 (rank2), n4 A=2,B=3 (rank3), and checked an additional n5 example; finite spectral checks supplement exact proof. Uniform implicit-function expansion is valid because s lies in compact [1,3].
